newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Suspected Moslem group members charged in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Moslem group members charged in Nigeria.

text.p: Forty-three suspected members of a Nigerian fundamentalist Shi'ite Moslem group arrested in December have pleaded not guilty to charges of illegal preaching and disturbing the peace, the national news agency reported on Sunday.

The Moslem Brothers group is campaigning for the imposition of Islamic Sharia law in Africa's most populous nation, although only about half the 100 million people are Moslems, mainly of the Sunni sect.

The News Agency of Nigeria quoted Abdulkadir Tambuwal, prosecutor for the state, as telling the area court judge in northern Sokoto state that all 43 were facing charges of unlawful assembly, illegal preaching, incitement and disturbance of public peace.
The defendants, detained since their arrests, pleaded not guilty to the charges, the agency said.
The judge adjourned the case to January 14 after the prosecutor said at the weekend hearing that the police needed more time to complete their investigations.

In September, two policemen and five Shi'ites were killed in northern Nigeria when supporters of the Moslem Brothers clashed with the police while demanding the release of their arrested leader, Sheikh Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky.
El-Zak-Zaky, a radical preacher, was arrested because of illegal publications and radio broadcasts, the police said. He was also alleged to have imported arms.
